title: The Interval-Length Price of Curvature Honesty under Block Interference

gap_reasons: The delivered results settle the finite-c honesty limit and several exact critical-window regimes, rather than the complete second-order frontier. At finite-positive effective-count transitions the normalized constants remain bracketed, and when the endpoint effective count diverges the smaller exact scale remains unidentified. The contribution is confined to noiseless, equal-size complete blocks with identical within-block outcomes and a public curvature cap, limiting its reach as an econometric method. The embedding concerns Jiang–Deng–Wang–Wang's Assumptions 1–2; the converse witnesses violate their additional third-increment condition, so the result establishes neither a contradiction of their inference theorem nor an empirical-network accuracy frontier ([source](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.04441v1)). The factor 1-alpha is attained through randomized retention and singleton outputs, making its operational interpretation specific to the stated expected-length objective. These scope restrictions and unresolved transition laws constrain the projected paper score; the framing does not falsely present the residual regimes as matched. proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived matching finite-c honesty limits, a universal finite-data honest interval, all-full-record randomized converses, and zero additive-oracle length, then added exact separated-level and diverging-depth critical cases and a no-size-only-normalization result. The mathematical review passed without findings, but the novelty review assigned subfield with paper-score ceiling 6.5 below field threshold 7.4. Finite-positive transitions and the endpoint-divergent smaller scale remain open; the SNIPE bank positioning issue remains disclosed, and formalization was never entered.
tldr: On heterogeneous complete blocks under one half-Bernoulli assignment, the exact additive-subclass price of curvature honesty is \(\ell(c,M,\alpha)=2(1-\alpha)Ma^2\), where \(a=0\) for \(0<c\le1/\log2\) and otherwise \(J(a)=1/c\). A finite-data honest original-record rule and an all-interval converse match this frontier. In the critical window, the single rule \(I^{\mathrm{crit}}\) also attains the exact separated effective-count phases and the exact diverging-deficit normalization with constant \(2(1-\alpha)M\); no positive normalization depending only on \(d\) works on every critical sequence. Three residuals remain: finite-positive effective-count transitions, the smaller exact scale when \(\rho_{m_n,d_n,0}\to\infty\), and the maximal subsequence-indexed phase diagram. The model is a new restricted subclass of Jiang--Deng--Wang--Wang's bounded-outcome, first- and product-weight second-increment class via \(w=1/d\). Only the lower bound transfers by inclusion; the exact upper frontier remains specific to these blocks. Nonzero tail witnesses fall outside their additional third-increment class along the stated growing-block regimes. The critical equality is included with zero first-order limit; \(c=\infty\) remains excluded because the ratio alone does not control oracle learning or recovery.
gap: Known-order interference estimation and generic spectral bias formulas do not evaluate the stated unconditional honest confidence-length objective. Classical Gaussian adaptation results do not determine the information radius of one random exposure coordinate per heterogeneous fixed table.
fill: Exact finite recovery and continuum agreement certificates, heterogeneous exposure means and coverage-calibrated retention provide the handles for evaluating the sequence-independent frontier. The deliverable is the exact finite-\(c\) value and its attaining rule, not an unevaluated recovery program.
